newsitem.title: USA: US House Banking Democrats issue technology report.
newsitem.headline: US House Banking Democrats issue technology report.

text.p: Consumer issues related to electronic banking should be a priority for the House Banking Committee in the next Congress, a report by the Democratic staff of the committee said Wednesday.

"The ramifications, particularly for consumers, of electronic banking on a large and escalating scale should be a high-level priority for the House Banking Committee in the next Congress," according to the report, which did not necessarily reflect the views of committee members.
Recommendations included letting the industry develop standards without legislation, but enacting legislation if public policy principles were not observed or concerns arose.
The report also recommended undertaking an analysis of federal consumer protection laws.

"Many of the Federal consumer protection laws are nearly 30 years old and they were not designed to deal with the effects of these new technologies," Rep. Henry Gonzalez of Texas, the committee's ranking Democrat, said in a statement.
Public policy principles should be adopted on privacy, disclosure, access and financial reliability issues, the report said.
